t.5.3.2: At night the mighty-spirited elephant among monkeys entered Laṅkā, the city rich in lovely groves and waters, protected by Rāvaṇa.
t.5.3.1: On the tall peak of Lamba, which looked like a great low-hanging rain cloud, the wise Hanumān, son of Māruta, summoned up his courage.
t.5.3.3: He beheld the city adorned with mansions resembling autumn clouds, resounding with a roar like that of the ocean and caressed by the winds from the sea.
t.5.3.4: The city was well guarded by strong, well-nourished forces, just like Viṭapāvatī, with lovely arches and turrets, and with gleaming white doors and gateways.
t.5.3.5: He beheld that city, frequented by serpents, well guarded and beautiful like Bhogavatī, the city of the Nāgas, covered with clouds flashing with lightning and visited by the paths of the stars.
t.5.3.6: He beheld the city resounding with the roar of fierce winds, like Indra's Amarāvatī, enclosed all around by a great wall of gold.
t.5.3.7: Having swiftly reached the city adorned with banners that jingled with clusters of little bells, he, delighted, went up to its rampart.
t.5.3.8: His heart filled with wonder, he gazed all around at the city, with its gates of Jāmbūnada gold whose raised platforms were fashioned of vaiḍūrya gems.
t.5.3.9: With gems, crystal and pearls, and with buildings adorned with jewelled floors, crowned with turrets of refined gold and gleaming spotless white like silver.
t.5.3.10: It was adorned with splendid mansions whose stairways were of beryl, whose inner grounds were strewn with crystal dust, and which were furnished with lovely quadrangles, so that they seemed to be soaring up into the sky.
t.5.3.11: In that place, loud with the cries of krauñca birds and peacocks, he beheld the city echoing on every side with the sounds of musical instruments and jingling ornaments, mingled with the calls of the royal swans that frequented it.
t.5.3.13: Having beheld that city Laṅkā of the lord of the Rākṣasas, beautiful, unsurpassed and endowed with prosperity, the valiant one reflected.
t.5.3.12: Then, beholding the city of Laṅkā, which resembled Vasvokasārā and seemed to have soared up into the sky, the monkey Hanumān rejoiced.
t.5.3.15: This land might also be accessible to Kumuda and Aṅgada, or to Suṣeṇa, the great monkey, and also to Mainda and Dvivida.
t.5.3.14: This city cannot be assailed by force by anyone else, guarded as it is by Rāvaṇa's troops bearing upraised weapons.
t.5.3.17: O mighty-armed one, having beheld the prowess of Rāghava and the valour of Lakṣmaṇa, the monkey became filled with delight.
t.5.3.16: Only the son of Vivasvat, the monkey Kuśaparvan, Ṛkṣa, Ketumāla, and I myself could find a way to reach this place.
t.5.3.19: That great monkey beheld the city of the lord of the Rākṣasas, its darkness dispelled by lamps and by great, shining mansions.
t.5.3.18: He saw her, the prosperous city, clad in jewels as her garments, with storehouses for her ear-ornaments and houses of machines for her breasts, adorned like a lovely young woman.
t.5.3.20: Having entered by night, the son of Māruta, endowed with courage, took to the great highway, which was resplendent with flowers and pearls.
t.5.3.22: Then Laṅkā blazed forth with the splendid mansions of the hosts of Rākṣasas, resembling white clouds, many-hued, laid out in the Padma and Svastika designs, and with Vardhamāna houses as well, richly adorned on every side.
t.5.3.23: The glorious one, who worked for the good of the king of the monkeys and moved about for the sake of Rāghava, saw that city adorned with bright garlands and ornaments, and he rejoiced.
t.5.3.21: The lovely city shone with its mansions, which resounded with loud peals of laughter accompanied by the sound of musical instruments, which resembled the thunderbolt and the goad, and which were adorned with diamond lattices, just as the sky shines with clouds.
t.5.3.24: He heard the sweet singing, adorned with notes in the three registers, of women abounding in intoxication, like that of the Apsarases in heaven.
t.5.3.25: He heard the jingling of girdles and the tinkling of anklets, and the sounds of footsteps on staircases in the mansions of the great-souled ones, and here and there the sounds of arms being slapped and of lion-like roars.
t.5.3.26: He saw yātudhānas devoted to the recitation of the Vedas, and also rākṣasas roaring, engaged in hymns of praise to Rāvaṇa.
t.5.3.27: He saw a great host of rākṣasas stationed there, blocking the royal highway, and in the central guard-post he saw the many spies of the rākṣasa lord.
t.5.3.28: He saw those consecrated for rites, some with matted locks and some with shaven heads, clad in garments of cowhide and deerskin, some armed with fistfuls of darbha grass, and likewise others whose weapons were fire-pits.
t.5.3.29: He saw some with mallets in their hands and others bearing staffs as weapons, some one-eyed and some many-eared, and some with swaying, pendulous breasts.
t.5.3.30: He saw some who were fearsome, some with crooked faces, some monstrous and some dwarfish; bowmen and swordsmen, warriors armed with śataghnīs and maces, others bearing excellent iron clubs in their hands, and others resplendent in variegated armour.
t.5.3.32: That great monkey saw rākṣasas whose weapons were spears and trees, others bearing paṭṭiśas and thunderbolts, and still others with slings and nooses in their hands.
t.5.3.31: He saw them neither too stout nor too lean, neither too tall nor too short; some misshapen, some of many forms, and some handsome and full of splendour.
t.5.3.33: He saw them wearing garlands and anointed with fragrant pastes, adorned with excellent ornaments, bearing sharp spears and wielding thunderbolts, mighty in strength.
t.5.3.34: The monkey, that great monkey, beheld the central guard, a hundred thousand strong and unwavering in its vigilance, completely enclosed by ramparts.
t.5.3.35: It resembled heaven itself, divine, resounding with heavenly sounds, ringing with the neighing of horses, and echoing likewise with the tinkling of ornaments.
t.5.3.36: It was filled with chariots, carriages and aerial cars, as well as with splendid elephants and horses, and with four-tusked elephants resembling masses of white clouds.
t.5.3.37: The monkey entered the house of the lord of the rākṣasas, adorned, with splendid gates, and guarded, enlivened by intoxicated beasts and birds.
